title: F&I Training - When The Customer Says “I Don’t Need A Warranty!”
summary: An F&I trainer coaches car salespeople on how to overcome a customer saying they don't need a warranty, using driving-habit questions, technology fear, and credit-card interest comparisons.

assertions.quote: it pays for all the breakdowns in technology all replaces repairs uh reprograms all those senses long after the factory warranty expires

verdicts.note: True as a general description, but contracts vary widely in what breakdowns are actually covered; 'all' overstates typical exclusion-laden contracts.

assertions.quote: why pay for repair at 18 or 19% or 14% on your credit card when you can have that repair paid for automatically at 6.9%

verdicts.note: The comparison only holds if a covered repair actually occurs and is approved; it ignores the warranty's own cost and the risk of claim denial.

assertions.quote: how long a customer is going to keep a car or how many miles they drive a year

verdicts.note: Plausible for many buyers, but average ownership length varies too much by buyer and vehicle to generalize confidently.
Lee & Venkataraman cite Polk data that the average U.S. vehicle age climbed from 9 years (2006) to 11.4 years (2013), "owners are holding on to vehicles longer, well past the base warranty."

assertions.quote: those infotainment centers in the vehicles they only last 2 years then they make new ones

verdicts.note: A single dealership manager's anecdote, not a verified industry-wide pattern.

assertions.quote: I love to ask questions prior to getting an fni presentation we call that the interview

verdicts.note: A sales-interview technique, not an independently tested predictor of actual warranty usage.
